items.snippet: U.S. smartphone shipments fell 9% year-over-year in the third quarter of 2026, and yet Apple grew its share of the market from 50% to 57%, according to the latest U.S. Market Monitor data from Counterpoint Research . items.title: HomeKit Weekly: Meross’s new presence sensor splits a room into three zones for Apple Home
items.snippet: Presence sensors tell Apple Home when someone is in a particular room, which is awesome for running automations based on that. They don’t tell it where in the room you are, though. That’s why these types of automations end up being all-or-nothing type things: you walk into a room, and every light comes on at full brightness, whether you came in to read at your desk or to grab something off the counter. The Meross MS605 splits its detection range into three distance zones, and each of them shows up in Apple Home as its own presence sensor so you can build automations around them. more…

items.title: Flaw in Linux NFS file sharing exposes servers to remote takeover
items.snippet: Researchers have found a critical flaw in the Linux kernel’s NFS file-sharing server that lets unauthenticated attackers obtain a root shell on affected systems. The flaw remained undetected in the kernel for 12 years, until two researchers, one using an AI agent, discovered it independently. NFS is typically used inside local networks, including in container networks in Kubernetes clusters and on build servers in development environments. However, it is also enabled on many embedded devices and in network-attached storage (NAS) devices which might be running older kernel versions and can only be patched with firmware updates. items.snippet: Broadcom on Tuesday reported almost two dozen new security vulnerabilities in VMware, adding to a lengthy list of fixes from this month alone.
